children: Shares of Nokia fell 2.8% in the afternoon session after the U.S. Commerce Department moved to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to lease Nvidia computing power from locations in other countries, CNBC reported, compounding hot wholesale inflation data and Nvidia’s leadership turmoil ahead of its earnings call under interim CEO Colette Kress.

Commerce’s action marks the first U.S. policy response to the scandal behind former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation.UBS trimmed its Nvidia price target to $240 from $300 ahead of the earnings report, citing potential export curbs on markets such as Singapore and Malaysia, CNBC noted. High-speed switches and custom interconnects ship in lumpy waves tied to data-center GPU deployments. If closing third-country compute loopholes curtails overseas cluster builds and Kress signals export bottlenecks during Nvidia’s earnings call, networking vendors face near-term valuation compression.
The shares were trading at $7.80, down 3.3% from the previous close.
What is the market telling us

Nokia’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 45 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Nokia is up 19.9% since the beginning of the year, but at $7.80 per share, it is still trading 53.7% below its 52-week high of $16.85 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Nokia’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,396.
